protocol.modelling_assumption: bladder stays in the scene as occluder + protected structure, rigidly displaced to a retracted position; never deleted; no deformation; urethra/bladder-neck continuity broken (limitation).
protocol.retraction_direction: d_r = normalise(cranial + anterior), patient frame as in prostate_access_wrist (anterior = plan B[:,2], cranial = lr x anterior with sign check: bladder centroid cranial-anterior of prostate)

admissibility.wall_note: inner wall is an open dome: a vertex is outside iff its ray to the interior reference hits the wall first

protocol.evaluation: identical to prostate_access_wrist: targets, ports grid, camera visibility, margins, polyline model; (a) conservative and (b) optimistic separate
protocol.selection: smallest admissible magnitude with >=1 triangulable target under (a)

port_plan.target_choice: max min-role reaching count; tie -> min |(t-c).lr|
port_plan.trio_rules: >=60 mm spacing pairwise + >=60 mm from ECM; meeting 20-100 deg
port_plan.side_rule: each role stays on its current arm side (sign of (port-c).lr)
port_plan.realisability: port_plan.json rules check; setup IK deferred to M3b build

selection.rule: smallest admissible magnitude with >=1 triangulable target under (a)

realisability.note: ports come from the same skin grid the current realised ports used; the setup-joint IK is plan_psm_ports work (M3b). depth_range/spacing rules are the planner criteria recorded in port_plan.json.

limitations: rigid displacement: no bladder deformation; urethra/bladder-neck continuity is broken geometrically
abdominal-wall penetration measured vs the 30 mm inner shell dome (open surface; verts outside its footprint do not count)
exploratory geometric feasibility only; no clinical claim
